questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Norm of a Vector With Respect to a Given Inner Product
questions.problem:
An inner product on $V={R}^{3}$ is defined as $⟨x,y⟩=2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.$ 
Calculate the norm of the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ under this inner product.
questions.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $v$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖=\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $‖v‖$ using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖ & =\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩} \\  & =\sqrt{2\cdot (3\cdot 3)+2\cdot (2\cdot 2)+(-3)\cdot (-3)} \\  & =\sqrt{18+8+9} \\  & =\sqrt{35}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2,$ equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(1)y(1)+x(2)y(2)+x(3)y(3).
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $p(t)=2-t+{t}^{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $p(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $p(t)=2-t+{t}^{2},$ we obtain

$$
p(1)=2,\,p(2)=4,\,p(3)=8.
$$

Computing $‖p(t)‖$ using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖ & =\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩} \\  & =\sqrt{p(1)p(1)+p(2)p(2)+p(3)p(3)} \\  & =\sqrt{[p(1)]^{2}+[p(2)]^{2}+[p(3)]^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{8}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+16+64} \\  & =\sqrt{84} \\  & =2\sqrt{21}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Norm of a Vector in an Inner Product Space of Continuous Functions
questions.problem:
Let $V=C[0,1]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[0,1],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $f(t)=2t+\sqrt{t}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(f(t))^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(2t+\sqrt{t})^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(4{t}^{2}+4t\sqrt{t}+t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={(\frac{4{t}^{3}}{3}+\frac{8{t}^{2}\sqrt{t}}{5}+\frac{{t}^{2}}{2})|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}+\frac{8}{5}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{103}{30}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{\frac{103}{30}}.
$$

questions.problem:
Let $V=C[-\pi ,\pi ]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[-\pi ,\pi ],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $f(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t.$
questions.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }(f(t))^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }\,{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }\,({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =(t+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}{2}){|}_{-\pi }^{\pi } \\  & =(\pi +\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡2\pi }{2})-((-\pi )+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(-2\pi )}{2}) \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we made use of the trigonometric identities

$$
{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t=1\,\text{and}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡2t=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t.
$$

Finally then,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖f(t)‖ & =\sqrt{2\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $f(t)=1-t.$
questions.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(f(t))^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(1-t)^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}({t}^{2}-2t+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={(\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}-{t}^{2}+t)|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{1}{3}-1+1)-(\frac{(-1)^{3}}{3}-(-1)^{2}+(-1)) \\  & =\frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{\frac{8}{3}}=2\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}.
$$

questions.problem:
An inner product on $V={R}^{3}$ is defined as $⟨x,y⟩=2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.$ 

Normalize the  vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ under this inner product.
questions.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $v$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖=\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨v,v⟩ & =2\cdot (3\cdot 3)+2\cdot (2\cdot 2)+(-3)\cdot (-3) \\  & =18+8+9 \\  & =35.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖ & =\sqrt{35}.\end{aligned}
$$

To normalize the vector $v$, we divide $v$ by its norm $‖v‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{v}{‖v‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{35}}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{35}}{35}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\frac{p(t)}{‖p(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{2+t}{5} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(2+t)\end{aligned}

questions.knowledge_point: Normalizing a Vector in an Inner Product Space
questions.problem:
Let $V=C[0,1]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[0,1],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Normalize the vector $f(t)=2-3t.$
questions.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{(2-3t)}^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\,(4-12t+9{t}^{2})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={(4t-6{t}^{2}+3{t}^{3})|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =4-6+3 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
‖f(t)‖=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1}}=1.
$$

To normalize the vector $f(t),$ we divide $f(t)$ by its norm $‖f(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\frac{f(t)}{‖f(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{2-3t}{1} \\  & =2-3t\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Norm of a Vector With Respect to a Given Inner Product
canonical_examples.problem:
An inner product on $V = \mathbb{R}^3$ is defined as $\langle \mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y} \rangle =  2x_1 y_1 + x_2 y_2 + 3x_3 y_3.$ 
Calculate the norm of the vector $[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ under this inner product.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $\mathbf v$ with respect to an inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖=\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $\|\mathbf{v}\|$ using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖ & =\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩} \\  & =\sqrt{2\cdot (3\cdot 3)+2\cdot 2+3\cdot (1\cdot 1)} \\  & =\sqrt{18+4+3} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Norm of a Vector in an Inner Product Space of Polynomials
canonical_examples.problem:
Let $V=\mathbb{R}_2[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2,$ equipped with the inner product

$$
\langle {x}(t), {y}(t) \rangle = x(1)y(1) + x(2)y(2) + x(3)y(3).
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector  $p(t) = 1 - t^2.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $p(t)$ with respect to an inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${p}(t) = 1-t^2,$ we obtain

$$
p(1)=0,\qquad 
p(2)= -3,\qquad 
p(3)=-8.
$$

Computing $\|p(t)\|$ using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖ & =\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩} \\  & =\sqrt{p(1)p(1)+p(2)p(2)+p(3)p(3)} \\  & =\sqrt{[p(1)]^{2}+[p(2)]^{2}+[p(3)]^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(0)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+(-8)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{0+9+64} \\  & =\sqrt{73}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Norm of a Vector in an Inner Product Space of Continuous Functions
canonical_examples.problem:
Let $V=\mathcal{C}\left[0,1\right]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $\left[0,1\right],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
\langle x(t),y(t) \rangle = \displaystyle\int_{0}^{1} x(t) y(t) \, \textrm{d}t.
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $f(t)= 2t-1.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is defined as

$$
\| f(t)\| = \sqrt{\langle  f(t),  f(t) \rangle}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(f(t))^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(2t-1)^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(4{t}^{2}-4t+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={(\frac{4{t}^{3}}{3}-2{t}^{2}+t)|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}-2+1 \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\| f(t)\| = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{3}} = \dfrac{\sqrt 3}{3}.
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Let $V=\mathcal{C}\left[0,\pi\right]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $\left[0,\pi\right],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
\langle x(t),y(t) \rangle = \displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi} x(t) y(t) \, \textrm{d}t.
$$

Normalize the vector $f(t)= 3t.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is defined as

$$
\| f(t)\| = \sqrt{\langle  f(t),  f(t) \rangle}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{(3t)}^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }9{t}^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & =3{t}^{3}\,{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =3{\pi }^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\| f(t) \|  = \sqrt{3\pi^3} = \pi \sqrt{3\pi}.
$$

To normalize the vector $f(t),$ we divide $f(t)$ by its norm $\| f(t) \| \mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\frac{f(t)}{‖f(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi \sqrt{3\pi }}\cdot 3t \\  & =\frac{t\sqrt{3}}{\pi \sqrt{\pi }}\end{aligned}
$$
